newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese minister demands Hariri reveal his worth.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese minister demands Hariri reveal his worth.

text.p: A Lebanese government minister challenged billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri and his colleagues to reveal their wealth, saying the new government was corrupt and would lead to scandals.

"The stench of the rotten files will increase," Druze leader Walid Jumblatt, minister for displaced people, told the Kuwait daily al-Rai al-Aam in an interview carried by Beirut newspapers on Tuesday.
"If Hariri thinks he can convince the Lebanese people that this government, in which he has retained the key finance and services portfolios, is an honest government, then he is wrong.
"It is not honest and we will only head for more scandals," Jumblatt said.
Jumblatt, who heads the Progressive Socialist Party, challenged Hariri, whose personal fortune is estimated at $4 bilion, and other officials to declare their wealth.

"He (Hariri) wants a social contract on his own terms, and we want it through the lifting of banking secrecy on the money and assets of all officials in power and in the country...If he is ready then I am ready," Jumblatt added.

Jumblatt was a close ally of Hariri during his first two governments between October 1992 and October 1996, but he has recently made slashing attacks on him, saying he has become too powerful and charging that his Beirut reconstruction plan has impoverished many Lebanese.

Beirut newspapers have recently reported scandals in public institutions. On October 28, a prosecutor charged six people with embezzling 15 billion Lebanese pounds from the sale of forged and genuine finance ministry revenue stamps.
Hariri has held the finance ministry portfolio since October 1992 and took over the posts and communications portfolio in the new government, leaving close colleagues to run them for him.
Jumblatt criticised Hariri's multi-billion dollar postwar reconstruction plan saying it concentrated on Beirut and neglected other areas.
Critics accuse Hariri of sinking Lebanon into debt to finance reconstruction and accuse him of lacking social policies but he has said the new government would make social issues a priority.
Asked if the new 30-member government could remedy the situation, Jumblatt said: "It is a tattered government and carries grave contradictions within itself..."
